children: Japan's preliminary 3Q data underwhelmed, and revisions are unlikely to change the overall picture of an economy struggling with fragile domestic demand and an unsteady external outlook, says Stefan Angrick at Moody's Analytics. Exports are unlikely to provide much of a lift in the coming quarters, as Japan doesn't benefit from the artificial-intelligence boom to the same extent as its peers. The rise in commodity prices and production costs due to the Middle East conflict makes it harder for Japanese manufacturers to compete. Meanwhile, wages aren't keeping pace with the broader economy, and consumers are struggling to make ends meet. "Without cost-of-living relief, stretched households would face another hit to purchasing power, materially raising the risk of recession," Angrick says. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
